assets.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Create ONE entirely new finished raster background for the alternate-history visual novel 九州沉浮录. Asset: early Qing imperial palace interior, scene qing_act4_b3_1, not a remake overlay or collage. Cinematic realistic environment painting, believable seventeenth-century Chinese wood and stone, finely detailed restrained film color, natural light. Wide landscape 16:9, target 1672x941. The scene is INSIDE the great imperial audience hall of the Forbidden City in Beijing, called Huangji Hall in the story, during a tense royal judicial confrontation. Depict only the empty architectural environment for character overlays: enormous dark-red timber columns, richly painted but subdued coffered beams, a proportionate raised imperial dais at the rear with a gilded dragon throne and small dark wooden imperial desk, dark stone paving. Two or three old paper dossiers and rolled judicial documents lie scattered at the side of the shallow steps, without any readable marks. Bronze incense vessels remain on solid stands; faint smoke. Light enters from side lattice doors, austere cool shadows with small amber light on the dais, serious tension but no battle damage. Slightly angled perspective from inside the hall, broad empty lower center floor, enough visible timber roof to convey the reverberating hall in the dialogue. No humans, silhouettes, captives, statues of humans, blood, flags, heraldry, modern objects, glass-chimney lamps, electric lighting, readable text, plaques, watermark or borders. This is historically informed alternate-fiction scenery, not a claim of exact reconstruction, and must not depict an outdoor palace gate or a modern tourist display.

assets.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Create ONE completely new finished raster background for the alternate-history Chinese visual novel 九州沉浮录. Asset: a final decision scene outside Taihe Hall in Beijing Forbidden City, not a collage or UI. Cinematic realistic environmental painting, finely detailed weathered stone and timber, plausible early Qing seventeenth-century palace, restrained natural film color. Wide landscape 16:9, target 1672x941. View across the enormous EMPTY stone forecourt from a subtle diagonal position, at human eye level, toward the great imperial hall. The central great hall has broad double-eaved imperial yellow glazed roofs and red wooden columns above a white stone triple terrace; side corridors recede into distance. The full hall should sit in the middle upper distance rather than fill the frame, and spacious grey flagstones occupy the lower third for game portraits and dialogue. The dramatic ceiling of layered storm clouds opens with a thin cool light toward the far side, soft warm reflection along roof edges. Time and fate seem suspended BEFORE a final political decision. No celebratory banners, troops or horses, no destruction, fire, rubble or symbols of a decided victory/defeat. Keep the architecture grounded and gravity plausible, not fantasy spires. No people, human silhouettes or human statues, no text or plaque or watermark, no modern flag, no tourist barriers, lamps, electric lights or modern objects. The story's A and C branches explicitly arrive at this same forecourt after earlier events in Jiangnan or the steppe; therefore depict the Beijing imperial palace only, not those earlier places. Historically informed alternate-fiction scenery, not an archaeological reconstruction.
